cards.objective: State the lobes of the right lung.
cards.front: How many lobes does the right lung have?

why.t: The right lung has three lobes; the left lung has two. Fissures separate them. The right lung is shorter and wider; the left holds a smaller volume, sharing space with the heart.

simpler.t: Your lungs take oxygen from the air into your blood and pass carbon dioxide out.

depth.t: Lobes: the right lung has three lobes; the left lung has two.
Cardiac notch: an indentation in the left lung that makes room for the heart.
Bronchopulmonary segments: divisions of a lobe, each with its own tertiary bronchus and artery.
Alveoli: tiny grape-like air sacs, about 200 micrometres across, with elastic walls.
Hilum: where the nerves enter the lung root and the two layers of pleura meet.

clinical.t: A baby born before enough surfactant is made. Without surfactant, the alveoli collapse during expiration.

trap.t: The left lung has two lobes and the cardiac notch; the right has three.

cards.source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 22.1 Organs and Structures of the Respiratory System; 22.2 The Lungs; 22.3; 22.7
